depiction.primary_object: closed padlock with a center circular keyhole
modifiers: diagonal slash from top-left to bottom-right
depiction.composition: single object in front view, crossed out by a diagonal bar

readings.meaning: unencrypted or insecure connection (no HTTPS / no SSL)
disable lock, remove password, or turn off protection
make public or remove privacy restrictions

ambiguity: Could be confused with an open shackle padlock ('unlocked'), though the slash specifically signals 'no lock / disabled security / insecure' rather than simply open; at very small sizes it can also resemble a crossed-out shopping bag.
task_intents: turn off disk or backup encryption
make private repository or document public

reasoning: A closed padlock crossed out by a diagonal slash universally signifies disabled locking, removed password protection, or an insecure/unencrypted state (such as browsers warning of missing HTTPS). It fits a solid niche of tech, admin, finance, and home tasks around removing locks, passwords, encryption, or credit freezes, though users must distinguish it from a standard open padlock ('unlock').
